Draft prototype for internal review. Figures are pre–company review; direction and position labels are provisional. Not for circulation.

Direction of travel, 2021–2025

Twenty-three US oil and gas companies, each measured against its own record. Company disclosures differ in definitions and boundaries, so this view compares direction, not levels.

Select any cell for its figures and notes.
Select a cell to see the series behind it.

Measured series use each company’s headline figure from its newest report; years are as printed. Directions compare the first and last two years (or first and last year where only three exist), with a ±10% band treated as flat. Counts under 10 events across the period get no direction. Totals that span an acquisition are marked as a series break rather than read as improvement or decline, unless the company itself restated earlier years onto the post-acquisition footprint. The federal records follow the same assets throughout: PHMSA incidents count only the pipeline operators a company held for the whole period, and EPA GHGRP emissions count only the facilities it held in all three reported years. Production counts growth by acquisition as growth and is labelled where acquired assets are included. Where a company’s newest report starts after 2021, earlier years come from its older reports, as originally published. Stated commitments compare what the company’s own documents said each year; the label compares the first year with the current entry, and “mixed” marks a path that strengthened in some years and weakened in others. Federal and state records added in October 2026: PHMSA enforcement cases and BSEE offshore violations are read as the company’s share of all cases the regulator opened each year, because those national totals fell over the period; BSEE offshore incidents are read per unit of offshore production the company operated; pipeline incidents are also shown per 1,000 miles of gas and hazardous liquid pipe (2022–2025); EPA methane intensity (onshore production) and the Texas flaring share are our ratios of government-reported volumes, on the same facilities or operators throughout. OSHA inspections and lobbying reports are shown as activity, with no good or bad reading; the EPA compliance record and DOE awards are snapshots, not trends.
